slot.brief: In YDSE, find the intensity (as a fraction of Imax) at a point whose path difference is an odd fraction of λ (e.g. λ/4 or 3λ/4), possibly requiring the position-to-path-difference conversion first.

stem: In a YDSE, coherent light gives individual slit intensities $4I_0$ and $I_0$. For $\lambda=600\ \text{nm}$, $d=0.60\ \text{mm}$, $D=1.2\ \text{m}$ and $y=0.45\ \text{mm}$, find $I(y)/I_{\max}$ using the small-angle approximation.

verdicts.working: The fringe spacing is \(\beta=\lambda D/d=1.2\,\text{mm}\), so the phase at \(y=0.45\,\text{mm}\) is \(2\pi y/\beta=3\pi/4\). Thus \(I/I_{\max}=(5+4\cos(3\pi/4))/9=(5-2\sqrt2)/9\).

working:
$\delta=dy/D=2.25\times10^{-7}\ \text{m}=3\lambda/8$; $\phi=2\pi\delta/\lambda=3\pi/4$. $I=5I_0+4I_0\cos\phi=(5-2\sqrt{2})I_0$; $I_{\max}=(2\sqrt{I_0}+\sqrt{I_0})^2=9I_0$.

Independent check: The fringe spacing is \(\beta=\lambda D/d=1.2\,\text{mm}\), so the phase at \(y=0.45\,\text{mm}\) is \(2\pi y/\beta=3\pi/4\). Thus \(I/I_{\max}=(5+4\cos(3\pi/4))/9=(5-2\sqrt2)/9\).
solution:
For two coherent slits, $I=I_1+I_2+2\sqrt{I_1I_2}\cos\phi$, with $\phi=2\pi dy/(\lambda D)=3\pi/4$.
$$\frac{I(y)}{I_{\max}}=\frac{4I_0+I_0+4I_0\cos(3\pi/4)}{(2\sqrt{I_0}+\sqrt{I_0})^2}=\frac{5-2\sqrt{2}}{9}$$
